places.name: Diamond Head (Lēʻahi) State Monument
places.ai_summary: Iconic crater hike with sweeping views of Waikīkī and Honolulu. A short, steep trail with stairs leads to the summit bunker. Go early for cooler temps and lighter crowds. Bring water and sun protection; parking is limited and timed reservations may be required during busy periods.
places.place_tip: Book a sunset slot for the best photos.

places.name: Waikīkī Beach
places.ai_summary: Famed crescent of sand backed by resorts, surf schools, and sunsets. Gentle waves suit beginners; promenades connect to dining and shopping. Vibrant in the evening with torchlighting and music. Ideal base for first-time visitors seeking easy access to tours and ocean activities.
places.place_tip: Bring reef‑safe sunscreen and a hat.

places.name: Pearl Harbor National Memorial
places.ai_summary: Somber, well‑curated memorials and museums telling the story of December 7, 1941. The USS Arizona Memorial boat program is the centerpiece. Plan time for exhibits and optional historic ships nearby. Book reservations ahead; morning slots are popular and sell out quickly.
places.place_tip: Buy tickets online to skip the queue.

attribution.title: Episode 4 of Kilauea's December 2024 eruption 2025-01-16
attribution.author: USGS/K. Lynn
attribution.description: View of the Kīlauea summit eruption in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, from the south rim of the caldera. The caldera wall behind the erupting vents is approximately 210 meters (690 feet) tall.  This morning, USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory field crews reported lava fountain heights of 50 meters (160 feet) and 40 m (140 feet) from north and south vents, respectively. At about 8:25 a.m. this morning, field crews reported that parts of the south vent collapsed, with an associated reduction of about half in south vent lava fountain height. Lava flow activity has remained confined to the southwest crater floor area near the active vents.
